item.title: Uber is the latest to be won over by Amazon’s AI chips
item.description: Uber is expanding its AWS contract to run more of its ride-sharing features on Amazon's chips. This is a thumb-of-the nose at Oracle and Google.

item.title: Anthropic ups compute deal with Google and Broadcom amid skyrocketing demand
item.description: Anthropic bulked up its compute deal with Google and Broadcom as the company has seen its run-rate revenue surge to $30 billion.

item.title: Google Maps can now write captions for your photos using AI
item.description: Gemini can now create captions when users are looking to share a photo or video.

item.title: 4 days left to save close to $500 on TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 passes
item.description: Four days left to save up to $482 on your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 ticket. These low rates will disappear on April 10 at 11:59 p.m. PT. Register now.

item.title: The AI gold rush is pulling private wealth into riskier, earlier bets
item.description: On a recent episode of Equity, we talked to Arena Private Wealth to explore a growing trend: family offices bypassing VCs to gain direct exposure to AI startups, turning them from passive investors into active participants.

item.title: AI startup Rocket offers vibe McKinsey-style reports at a fraction of the cost
item.description: Rocket's new AI platform combines strategy, product building, and competitive intelligence, aiming to move beyond code generation.

item.title: OpenAI alums have been quietly investing from a new, potentially $100M fund
item.description: Zero Shot, a new venture capital fund with deep ties to OpenAI, is aiming to raise $100 million for its first fund. It has already written some checks.

item.title: Google quietly launched an AI dictation app that works offline
item.description: Google's new offline-first dictation app uses Gemma AI models to take on the apps like Wispr Flow.

item.title: Iran threatens ‘Stargate’ AI data centers
item.description: Iran said it will target U.S.-linked data centers with new missile strikes, as the war between the U.S. and Iran escalates.

item.title: OpenAI’s vision for the AI economy: public wealth funds, robot taxes, and a four-day workweek
item.description: OpenAI proposes taxes on AI profits, public wealth funds, and expanded safety nets to address job loss and inequality, blending redistribution with capitalism as policymakers debate AI’s economic impact.

item.title: Startup Battlefield 200 applications open: a chance for VC access, TechCrunch coverage, and $100K
item.description: Nominate your startup, or one you know that deserves the spotlight, and finish the process by applying. Selected 200 have a chance at VC access, TechCrunch coverage, and $100K for Startup Battlefield 200. Applications close on May 27.

item.title: How to use the new ChatGPT app integrations, including DoorDash, Spotify, Uber, and others
item.description: Learn how to use Spotify, Canva, Figma, Expedia, and other apps directly in ChatGPT.

item.title: Ticket savings of up to $500 this week for TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
item.description: Starting today, you have 5 days to save nearly $500 on your ticket to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. This offer disappears Friday, April 10, at 11:59 p.m. PT. Register here to secure these low rates.

item.title: Spain’s Xoople raises $130 million Series B to map the Earth for AI
item.description: The company is also announcing a deal with L3Harris to build the sensors for Xoople's spacecraft.

item.title: Copilot is ‘for entertainment purposes only,’ according to Microsoft’s terms of use
item.description: AI skeptics aren’t the only ones warning users not to unthinkingly trust models’ outputs — that’s what the AI companies say themselves in their terms of service.

item.title: Can orbital data centers help justify a massive valuation for SpaceX?
item.description: On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, we debated Elon Musk's vision for data centers in space.

item.title: In Japan, the robot isn’t coming for your job; it’s filling the one nobody wants
item.description: Driven by labor shortages, Japan is pushing physical AI from pilot projects into real-world deployment.

item.title: Anthropic says Claude Code subscribers will need to pay extra for OpenClaw usage
item.description: It’s about to become more expensive for Claude Code subscribers to use Anthropic’s coding assistant with OpenClaw and other third-party tools.

item.title: Anthropic is having a moment in the private markets; SpaceX could spoil the party
item.description: Glen Anderson, president of Rainmaker Securities, says the secondary market for private shares has never been more active — with Anthropic the hottest trade around, OpenAI losing ground, and SpaceX's looming IPO poised to reshape the landscape for everyone.

item.title: OpenAI executive shuffle includes new role for COO Brad Lightcap to lead ‘special projects’
item.description: In addition to Lightcap's new role, OpenAI CMO Kate Rouch will be stepping away from the company to focus on cancer recovery, with a plan to return when her health allows.
